rv.q: Terry Johnson's revival has energy and charm, with Tim Shortall's design evoking the period's extravagant fashions.
The Libertine is an enjoyable, but rather unfulfilling play.
Not a full-on flop all told but be warned, if you go seeking after the elixir of lusty excitement you may end up feeling you've but quaffed a cup of Earl Grey.
But what, you wonder at the close, is the point of this? The story of his life is shapeless and as a dramatic experience it ultimately feels a mite unsatisfying.
